title: Concurrent activation requests for the same framework/project produce a single ClientFramework document
description: addToProject uses ClientFramework.findOneAndUpdate({organizationId, projectId, frameworkId}, {...}, {upsert:true, new:true}) specifically to make double-click / concurrent-tab activation atomic instead of creating duplicate rows.
preconditions: Framework is active in the catalog and licensed for the org
steps: Fire two POST /compliance-frameworks/projects/:projectId/frameworks requests with the same frameworkId in quick succession
expectedResult: Exactly one ClientFramework document exists with status 'active'; no duplicate-key error and no second document created.

title: Activating an unlicensed framework returns 403 LICENSING_REQUIRED without creating a ClientFramework record
preconditions: Framework exists and is status 'active' in the catalog, but is not in the org's licensed set
expectedResult: Response is 403 with body { success: false, error: 'LICENSING_REQUIRED', message: ... }. No ClientFramework document is created for this org/project/framework.

title: A failed complianceSync.activateFramework leaves the ClientFramework doc already upserted to 'active' before the seed error is raised
description: In addToProject, the ClientFramework upsert (setting status:'active') happens BEFORE the try/catch around complianceSync.activateFramework. If the seed of client requirements/controls throws, the caller receives a 503 telling them to retry — but the ClientFramework record is already status:'active' with no ClientRequirement/ClientControl rows behind it. Documents current behavior: the framework will appear 'Active' in the UI with a compliance map that has zero controls until retried.
preconditions: complianceSync.activateFramework is mocked/forced to throw (e.g. DB write failure during seeding)
steps: POST /compliance-frameworks/projects/:projectId/frameworks for a licensed framework while activateFramework is forced to fail
Navigate to /grc-framework and check the framework's displayed status
expectedResult: API returns 503 'Framework activation could not seed client requirements and controls. Retry activation.' However the ClientFramework doc already exists with status:'active' — the framework shows as Active in the catalog with an empty compliance map until the caller retries activation. Flagged as a partial-failure state worth hardening (wrap the upsert and seed in one transaction, or roll back the upsert on seed failure).

title: Deactivating a framework whose license was revoked (status='license_revoked') succeeds and sets status to 'archived'
preconditions: A ClientFramework record has status 'license_revoked' (set by a prior license-revocation cascade)
expectedResult: Request succeeds (200) and the ClientFramework document's status becomes 'archived' with archivedAt/archivedBy set — it is no longer an orphaned dead-end record that can never be cleanly removed.

title: available-frameworks controlCount is sourced from active leaf FrameworkRequirement counts, matching the count shown post-activation
description: availableFrameworks() deliberately counts FrameworkRequirement leaf nodes (isLeaf:true, status:'active'), the same source ClientRequirement rows are materialized from on activation — not the older, drifted FrameworkControl collection getControls() uses — so the catalog's advertised control count doesn't change once the framework is activated.
preconditions: A framework has 42 active leaf FrameworkRequirement docs but a different count in the legacy FrameworkControl collection
steps: GET /compliance-frameworks/projects/:projectId/available-frameworks and note controlCount for the framework (pre-activation)
expectedResult: Both counts equal 42 — the pre-activation catalog count and the post-activation compliance map count agree, using the FrameworkRequirement source in both places.

title: PATCH excluded-controls persists a mixed valid/invalid ID list, keeping only the valid subset
steps: PATCH /compliance-frameworks/projects/:projectId/frameworks/:id/excluded-controls with excludedRequirementIds containing 2 valid leaf requirement IDs of this framework and 1 invalid/foreign ID
expectedResult: Response returns excludedRequirementIds (and the compatibility alias excludedControlIds) containing only the 2 valid IDs; the invalid one is dropped without erroring the whole request.

title: getControlUclDetail filters automated checks to only the cloud providers enabled in the project's pscanner_configs
description: When a projectId query param is supplied, getControlUclDetail reads pscanner_configs for that project and filters the control's checks down to providers with providers.<name>.enabled true. Without a matching config, all checks for the control are returned unfiltered.
preconditions: A control has automated checks from both aws and azure providers
The project's pscanner_configs has aws.enabled=true, azure.enabled=false
expectedResult: Only the aws-provider checks are present in the response's checks array; azure checks for the same control are excluded.

title: A user with org-level compliance.read but no membership on the target project is rejected on /projects/:projectId/frameworks
description: PLAC Phase 2 fix: requireProjectMembership() now runs on every /projects/:projectId/* compliance-frameworks and client-compliance route, closing a gap where only org membership (assertOrgAccess) was ever checked, never actual project membership.
preconditions: User has the compliance.read permission at the org/role level
User is NOT a member of projectId (no ProjectMember row) and is not an org-level project.admin
expectedResult: 403 Forbidden — org-level compliance.read alone is not sufficient; project membership (or org project.admin bypass) is required.

title: listRequirements with limit=0 fetches up to the 2000-row cap without a divide-by-zero in pagination.pages
description: limit=0 means 'fetch all up to MAX_LIMIT' for internal compliance-map use. The fix uses effectiveLimit (never 0) in the pages calculation instead of the raw query param, which previously produced pages: Infinity.
steps: GET /compliance-frameworks/projects/:projectId/client-requirements?limit=0 for a framework with 300 requirements
expectedResult: pagination.limit is 2000 (the MAX_LIMIT), pagination.pages is a finite integer (1), and data contains all 300 requirements — not Infinity/NaN.

title: getRequirementWithAssets returns both direct-attached and UCL-chain-attached resources for a single requirement
description: A resource can reach a requirement two ways: directly (doc.evidenceIds/policyIds/certificationIds/vendorControlIds/riskIds) or via the UCL chain (requirement -> requirement_ucl_mapping_v2 -> a ClientControl sharing that uclId -> that control's own policyIds/vendorControlIds/integrationEvidenceIds/trustCertificationIds/riskIds). 'direct' wins when a resource is reachable both ways (resolveSource checks direct sourceMap entries first).
preconditions: Requirement R has one directly-attached policy P1
R maps to UCL U1, and a ClientControl for U1 has vendor V1 and (also) P1 attached
expectedResult: resources[] contains P1 with source:'direct' (not 'control', despite also being reachable via the UCL-linked ClientControl) and V1 with source:'control' and a populated uclInfo object.
